name: Temperature Converter
description: Convert temperature between Celsius, Fahrenheit, Kelvin, and Rankine instantly, with impossible-value detection below absolute zero.

faq.question: Why is temperature different from a normal unit converter?
faq.answer: Length and weight scales all share a common zero point (0 m is "no length" in every unit), so conversion is just multiplication. Celsius and Fahrenheit have different zero points — 0°C is 32°F, not 0°F — so conversion needs both a scaling factor and an offset, not just a factor.

faq.question: What are Kelvin and Rankine?
faq.answer: Both are absolute scales, where 0 means absolute zero — the coldest physically possible temperature — rather than an arbitrary reference point like water freezing. Kelvin uses Celsius-sized degrees (used throughout science); Rankine uses Fahrenheit-sized degrees (occasionally used in older US engineering contexts).

faq.question: Why does entering a very negative number sometimes show an error?
faq.answer: Nothing can be colder than absolute zero (-273.15°C / -459.67°F / 0 K), so a value that would convert to below that is flagged as physically impossible rather than silently shown as, say, a negative Kelvin reading.
